subject: biology
title: Lipids & Proteins Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll dive into lipids and proteins — fats, phospholipids, and the four levels of protein structure.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Biological Molecules — triglycerides, phospholipids, ester bonds, peptide bonds, and primary to quaternary protein structure.
final_note: You learned that triglycerides are glycerol + 3 fatty acids joined by ester bonds, phospholipids have a polar head, and proteins fold through four levels of structure.

concepts.def: Glycerol + 3 fatty acids joined by ester bonds
Bond between -OH (glycerol) and -COOH (fatty acid), releasing water
Glycerol + 2 fatty acids + phosphate group — forms bilayers
Bond between amino group and carboxyl group of two amino acids
Variable side chain that defines each amino acid's properties
Multiple polypeptide chains joined into a functional protein (e.g. haemoglobin)

walkthroughs.body_html:
A triglyceride = 1 glycerol + 3 fatty acids.

Each fatty acid attaches via an ester bond, releasing 3 H₂O molecules in total.

Saturated = no C=C, straight chain (animal fats, solid).
Unsaturated = one or more C=C, kinked (plant oils, liquid).

Phospholipids replace one fatty acid with a phosphate group, giving a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails — the basis of the cell membrane bilayer.

An amino acid has 4 parts attached to a central C:
- amino group (-NH₂)
- carboxyl group (-COOH)
- hydrogen (-H)
- R group (variable)

There are 20 different R groups → 20 amino acids.

Two amino acids join by condensation, forming a peptide bond between -NH₂ and -COOH. Many = a polypeptide.

1° Primary — the amino acid sequence.
2° Secondary — α-helix or β-pleated sheet, held by H-bonds.
3° Tertiary — 3D fold from R-group interactions: H-bonds, ionic, disulfide bridges, hydrophobic.
4° Quaternary — multiple polypeptides joined (e.g. haemoglobin = 4 chains + 4 haem).

Shape determines function — change one R group and the protein may break.

numericals.hint: One H₂O per ester bond formed
